release.content: observability 0.5.0 was released on 2026-11-27 from commit 59e20e37452d1a4ee2ed9420c390d99daf858704 with these changes.

rows: The uptime probe records: with UPTIME_TABLE set, as the Cloud Run job observability-uptime that Cloud Scheduler starts every five minutes, each run appends one row per target, up or not, to BigQuery's observability.uptime_probes as the job's attached account (no key), keeps no state and posts nothing, and exits 1 when any target failed; the new fact uptime_probes reads them, and the rules uptime_down (critical: a target's newest failed_runs probes, 2 by default, all failed) and uptime_silent (critical: no probe row for silent_minutes, 15 by default) go to Slack through the notifier; deploy.yml sets the job's image and settings once UPTIME_CLOUD_RUN is set; targets are probed all at once
inbox_stale (version 2) reads the newest sweep's report and rejected_files (version 2) the newest listing's, up to ten hours back, as a pass on the files storage told of lists nothing

observability thresholds --upgrade prints OBSERVABILITY_THRESHOLDS at the latest version; version 1 is read through the chained transformers, sender_silent's silent_minutes becoming the tight and cycle tiers' and ingest_silent's its margin_minutes

Senders have tiers: OBSERVABILITY_SENDERS takes tight, idle and cycle (always is cycle's old name), and OBSERVABILITY_THRESHOLDS version 2 their numbers (deadline_seconds, heartbeat_seconds, silent_minutes; tight 30/300/10, idle 28800/28800/540, cycle 120/120/10); sender_silent (version 3) and the trends page call a sender silent after its tier's silent_minutes, and ingest_silent (version 3) gives each project its quickest sender's window and a margin_minutes

The incidents fact reads Cloud Monitoring's SLA incidents (observability.incidents_view), and sla_incident (critical) and sla_incident_warning give each open incident a signal until it closes, a sender's under its sender_silent subject (project/sender) and a site's under its service, so NOTIFIER_ROUTES routes them as before
